meaning: A machine that boots the MCU does exactly four writes before AUTO: clear JOB int, clear MMU int, UNMASK JOB int (write 0), then MCU_CONTROL=2. It then polls JOB_INT_RAWSTAT (0x1000) bit31, not the masked STAT (0x100c). No hw-issues, no CSF_CONFIG, no L2_CONFIG, no ASN_HASH, no soft reset inside this function.
action: Compare against hakios.mali610.c:3131-3133 (mask written 0xffffffff, i.e. everything masked before start_mcu) and :3897 (polls 0x100c). Both differ. See entry 'R1'.

quote: gpuWrite(kJobIntMask, 0);   // polled
meaning: Mask register bit = ENABLE bit; 0 means unmasked. This driver unmasks everything so that its RAWSTAT poll (line 545) can see bit31 arrive.
action: hakios.mali610.c:3132 writes mwr(kJobIntMask, 0xffffffffu) in gpu_irq_mask_prestart(), which runs unconditionally at :4641, before start_mcu(). Flip to 0 (or re-write 0 at the top of start_mcu) so RAWSTAT is observable.

quote:
#define JOB_INT_RAWSTAT 0x1000
#define JOB_INT_CLEAR   0x1004
#define JOB_INT_MASK    0x1008
#define JOB_INT_STAT    0x100c
#define   JOB_INT_GLOBAL_IF  BIT(31)
meaning: 0x1000 is the raw latch, 0x100c is the masked view. 0x100c = RAWSTAT & ~MASK. With MASK bit31 set, reading 0x100c can never show GLOBAL_IF regardless of whether the MCU raised it.
action: This is the mechanism behind R1. It explains 'we never see GLOBAL_IF' without requiring the MCU to be dead, but it does NOT explain a version word that still holds the sentinel.

meaning: PanTGor writes the events it wants into MASK. The handler at line 308 reads 'gpu_read(RAWSTAT) & pirq->mask', i.e. it filters RAWSTAT itself rather than trusting STAT.
action: Second independent source for the MASK polarity. Combined with the kbase disassembly (0x3b7c0 writes 0 then 0x3ba60 writes 0xffffffff to 0x1008) the polarity is settled.

quote: gpuWrite(kMcuControl, 2);   // MCU_CONTROL_AUTO
meaning: Only AUTO (2) is ever written to start. No ENABLE (1). Matches kbase, where the whole module writes only {0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2} at offset 0x700.
action: hakios.mali610.c:3843 already writes kMcuControlAuto. No change. Note :3837 writes kMcuControlEnable=1 on a probe path - check it does not run before AUTO in the current build.

quote:
if (!softReset()) return;
printf("mali: soft reset done\n");
meaning: Ken-u resets the block (GPU_CMD = 0x101, kSoftReset at line 79) BEFORE L2 power-up and before the firmware is loaded. Its MCU therefore starts from a known reset state.
action: hakios.mali610.c only resets under !gMaliCold, and gMaliCold defaults to 1 (:522), so the default path never resets. The reason to skip it is documented at :3618-3624 (panthor never resets on the fw_init path). This is a path difference, not a proven defect. Do not flip blindly.

quote:
gpuWrite64(asReg(as, kAsLockaddr), 63);   // lock_region(0, ~0): width 64 - 1, start 0
if (!asCommand(as, kAsCmdLock) || !asCommand(as, kAsCmdFlushMem) || !asReady(as)) { ... }
meaning: Ken-u sends LOCK then FLUSH_MEM then UPDATE on AS0. This project deliberately sends only UPDATE (hakios.mali610.c:2885-2887 explains the removal).
action: Platform/design difference. Both reach UPDATE successfully on this board (AS0 fault status 0, MMU int 0x10000 = REQ_COMPLETE). Not the variable.

quote: const uint64_t transcfg = (2ull << 24) /* PTW_MEMATTR_WB */ | (1ull << 30) /* PTW_RA */ | 6 /* AARCH64_4K */ | (static_cast<uint64_t>(55 - vaBits) << 6);
meaning: With vaBits=48 this is 0x420001c6 (includes INA_BITS(55-48)=0x1c0 in bits 11:6). The project writes 0x42000006 instead, matching kbase.
action: Both values have been tried on this board and both let AS0 UPDATE complete. This is not a distinguishing variable for the MCU symptom. task description already says so - confirmed here from the source.

quote: constexpr uint64_t kMemAttr = 0x4c4c4c4c9c4c9f4cULL;
meaning: Ken-u installs panthor's mair_to_memattr() table (index 0 = 0x4c). This project installs kbase's seven-entry table 0x00084c8d888d8f88 (index 0 = 0x88), documented at hakios.mali610.c:864-883.
action: Unverified which is correct on MT6895. Both are derived from a real driver. If firmware sections are mapped with index 0, the two tables disagree about what index 0 means (0x4c = NC vs 0x88 = impl-def cached). Worth one A/B run, cost is one boot.

meaning: Ken-u skips protected-mode sections entirely, matching panthor_fw.c:531-534 ('Firmware protected mode entry not be supported, ignoring').
action: hakios.mali610.c:1069-1072 only prints 'is protected-mode, mapped with ordinary memory' and then DOES map it (:1074 onwards, no continue). The task description says '3 PROT skipped' but the code maps them. Reconcile code and log text before trusting either.

topic: PROT section flags have no ZERO bit
quote: sec6/sec7/sec8: flags 0x0000002b va 0x3000000-0x3040000 data 0 (PROT, no bit31)
meaning: The three protected sections carry R|W|cached|PROT but NOT the ZERO flag (bit31). panthor_fw.c:403 only memsets the tail when ZERO is set, so nothing requires the host to zero them. They are just unmapped-by-design regions.
action: Mapping them with ordinary zeroed pages is harmless (mem_alloc uses KMA_ZERO at :737). Skipping them is also harmless. This cannot be the cause of MCU not executing - drop it from the candidate list.

quote: version=0x00000000 features=0x0 input_va=0x04002000 output_va=0x04003000 group_num=8 group_stride=0xa0 perfcnt_size=0 instr_features=0x71
meaning: The image ships a fully populated glb_control except version==0. So version is the only word that proves execution, which is exactly what the sentinel technique at hakios.mali610.c:3955 exploits.
action: Keep the sentinel. Note output_va here is 0x04003000 while Ken-u's board read 0x04006000 - different firmware layout, both inside the 4 MiB shared region, so no action (globalInterface follows control->output_va anyway).

quote: VA 0: MSP = 0x02040000, Reset = 0x010018ed (bit0 = 1, Thumb)
meaning: Confirms the task description. Reset target lies in section 1 (va 0x1000000-0x1010000, flags 0x0d = rwx cached), leaf 1 at 0x01001000.
action: The project already found and fixed a 16K-PAGE_SIZE mapping hole that left section 1 25% mapped (:1170-1191). Verify the fix is in the built kernel: a walk log for VA 0x1000000 should show a leaf whose low two bits are 11.

meaning: The full field set and the toggle-from-ack rule. Identical to what this project already does at hakios.mali610.c:4196-4204.
action: No change needed. Our version additionally does mem_flush(&gShared->mem) at :4207 because our shared section is cacheable - that is more correct than Ken-u, which maps it non-cacheable.

quote: printf("mali: present: shader %#x tiler %#x l2 %#x stack %#x; threads %u features %#x; coherency features %#x\n", ... gpu(kCoherencyFeatures));
meaning: 0x300 is read for reporting only. grep for 0x304 across the whole 3155-line file returns zero hits: Ken-u never writes GPU_COHERENCY_PROTOCOL.
action: On MT6895 kbase DOES write 0x304 (work-notes-kbase-mcu-boot-sequence.md:64, at 0x3b9a0). Platform difference. This project writes 31 only under !gMaliCold or mali_cohnone (:3174), so the default path leaves it alone - same as Ken-u. Fine.

quote: gpuWrite(kCmd, 0x103);
meaning: Ken-u does issue GPU_COMMAND_TIME_ENABLE, but only inside its clock probe block (comment at :3108 'GPU_COMMAND_TIME_ENABLE starts it'). It is for measuring MHz, not for booting the MCU.
action: hakios.mali610.c never writes 0x103. Adding it has diagnostic value only: if the GPU cycle counter (0x88..0x94) advances, the clock reaches the MCU domain. This is not a fix.

quote:
gpuWrite(kL2PwrOn, mask);
const bool ok = waitUs(20000, [mask] { return (gpu(kL2Ready) & mask) == mask; });
meaning: Ken-u waits only for READY, never for PWRTRANS to fall. PWRTRANS is printed, not tested.
action: hakios.mali610.c:3222-3237 tests PWRTRANS first. We are stricter. Nothing to borrow.

topic: nothing MTK-specific exists in this driver
quote: grep -c -i for: csf_config / asn / 0x2c0 / L2_CONFIG / 0x48 / ipi / mbox / gpueb / pdc / mtcmos / 0xf00 / shader_pwron  =>  all zero
meaning: A driver that boots Mali-G610 CSF on RK3588 writes none of CSF_CONFIG(0xF00), L2_CONFIG(0x48), ASN_HASH(0x2C0), SHADER_PWRON(0x180), nor any hw-issue workaround. So none of these can be claimed as the missing step by analogy.
action: Remove 'we forgot hw-issues / CSF_CONFIG / ASN_HASH / L2_CONFIG' from the candidate list. If MT6895 needs them it must be argued from MTK's own driver, not from Ken-u.

quote: AIR shader translation support. Offline compilation supports original UI shaders. The runtime uses metal2vulkan and Turnip.
meaning: It compiles Metal AIR to NIR and feeds IR3 (Adreno's backend). It is an Adreno-route component.
action: Not usable for the Mali route. PanVK needs NIR -> Valhall, which lives in Mesa's panfrost compiler. Ken-u's stack goes metal2vulkan -> SPIR-V -> PanVK instead. No action.

quote: GPU-related repos returned: Adreno740, AdrenoMetal, AdrenoFirmware, AdrenoPM4, Adreno610, Adreno830 - all Qualcomm. Zero Mali repos in UniXNU org.
meaning: Ken-u/Mali is the only Mali implementation in the entire UniXNU ecosystem. There is no independent second source to cross-check its bring-up against.
action: Any claim of the form 'other UniXNU devices do X for GPU' is only available for Adreno. Cross-checking the CSF path must fall back to panthor (upstream) and to MTK's own kbase.

topic: the one bring-up trap Ken-u documents
quote: MCU 的队列接口和 suspend buffer 必须放在 MCU 的 shared region（0x04000000–0x08000000）里 ... 放到 0x10000000 时 CSG 能启动、但 stream 永远不 ACK START，AS0 上报「写 0x1000 的 translation fault」
meaning: Firmware masks MCU-side addresses with 0x0fffffff. Anything outside 0x04000000-0x08000000 aliases and faults. Cost Ken-u 4 rounds.
action: Relevant only after GLOBAL_IF is seen. Our shared section is at 0x04000000 (MALI_SHARED_VA :992), so we are inside the region. Also: our fw declares output_va 0x04003000 - inside. No action now, but keep for the M2 stage.

topic: no kernel bring-up detail in MaliMetal
quote: grep -i "mcu|firmware|power domain|soft reset" over 541 lines -> only one hit, about per-client VM/group virtualisation
meaning: The MaliMetal notes are entirely user-space (PanVK build, metal2vulkan, sandbox grants, frame rate, backboardd crashes). The task's hypothesis that this file holds more bring-up detail is false.
action: Do not spend more time on MaliMetal for CSF bring-up. The kernel-side detail is all in Ken-u/Mali's own docs/notes.zh-CN.md and its Mali.cpp.
